history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Sikh gurdwara (tradition: Sikhism) built by the Army authorities at a reported cost of Rs 27,118 to commemorate the 21 Sikh soldiers of the 36th Sikh Regiment who were killed defending Fort Saragarhi on the Samana Ridge (North-West Frontier) against roughly 10,000 Pathans on 12 September 1897. Declared open in 1904 by Sir Charles Rivaz, the then Lieutenant Governor of Punjab. The gurdwara is surrounded by cannons and carries the names of the 21 martyrs inscribed on its walls; every year on 12 September a religious congregation is held in the morning with an ex-servicemen reunion in the evening. One of three Saragarhi memorial gurdwaras (Saragarhi, Firozpur, Amritsar). Coordinates are geocoder-matched to a Firozpur Cantt gurdwara address with moderate relevance — approximate, verify.

name: Saragarhi Memorial Temple
town_description: Firozpur (Ferozepur) is a historic border city in Punjab near the India-Pakistan border, known for its military heritage — the Saragarhi Memorial Gurdwara, the Barki Memorial of the 1965 war, and the National Martyrs Memorial at Hussainiwala, where Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were cremated.
